3567575.background: Alaska uses a top-four nonpartisan primary followed by ranked-choice general. Incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan seeks a third term; former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola, who lost the House seat narrowly in 2024, entered the Senate race. Several minor candidates split remaining votes, so margins between leaders depend on turnout.

actors.name: Mary Peltola
actors.public: Former US Representative (2022-2025), Yupik, strong personal brand, cross-party appeal on fisheries and rural issues; won 2022 special and general, lost 2024 to Begich by about 3 points.
actors.private: Primary is a low-stakes signalling contest; she wants a strong first-place or close-second showing to prove viability and attract donors, but saves money for November.

actors.name: Dan Sullivan
actors.public: Two-term Republican incumbent, Marine reservist, large war chest, backed by state and national GOP, aligned with Trump administration on energy and Alaska development.
actors.private: Wants to finish first in the primary to blunt momentum narratives; Republican consolidation behind him limits vote split; vulnerable to anti-Trump midterm mood.

actors.name: Alaska primary electorate
actors.public: Low-turnout August primary skewing older and more Republican; 2022 and 2024 primaries showed fragmented fields with minor candidates taking several percent.
actors.private: Undecided independents and rural Native voters turn out unevenly; Democratic-leaning voters may be underrepresented relative to November.

events.name: Credible third Republican or independent candidate draws significant share
Late-count absentee ballots shift margin by more than 2 points after election night
Major national scandal or event shifts Alaska mood before Aug 18

3591977.background: GA-14 in northwest Georgia is deeply Republican (Trump +35 range). Marjorie Taylor Greene resigned in January 2026; a 2026 special election filled the seat. Georgia requires a majority in the general election or a December runoff; races usually feature only one Republican and one Democrat.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Nominee in a district Republicans win with roughly two-thirds of the vote; special-election winner or primary victor backed by local GOP and Trump-aligned groups.
actors.private: Main risk is ballot fragmentation, not defeat; would avoid any independent or Libertarian candidacy that splits the conservative vote.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Underfunded challenger in a safe-red seat; 2024 Democrat got about 35 percent.
actors.private: Aims to improve margin in a favourable midterm year but has no path to a majority.

actors.name: Georgia Secretary of State
actors.public: Certifies results; Georgia has run majority-runoff general elections for decades.
actors.private: Ballot access for third parties is hard in Georgia House races, so fields usually stay two-candidate.

events.name: Third-party or independent candidate qualifies for ballot
Results delayed past March 2027 by litigation

3591982.background: GA-09 in northeast Georgia is one of the state's most Republican districts; Rep. Andrew Clyde (R) has held it since 2021 with about two-thirds of the vote. Georgia requires a general-election majority or a runoff; House races usually have only two candidates.

actors.name: Andrew Clyde or Republican nominee
actors.public: Freedom Caucus-aligned incumbent, gun-store owner, wins general elections easily; faced primary challengers before.
actors.private: Expects a comfortable win; only concern is a primary upset or retirement producing an open seat, neither of which changes the majority math much.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Low-profile challenger in a district Trump won by over 35 points.
actors.private: No realistic path; running to build party presence.

actors.name: Georgia ballot-access rules
actors.public: Independent and minor-party congressional candidates need petitions of 5 percent of registered voters, rarely achieved.
actors.private: Effectively guarantees two-candidate fields in most districts.

3591988.background: GA-03 in west-central Georgia is safely Republican; Rep. Brian Jack (R), a former Trump aide, won the open seat in 2024 with about two-thirds of the vote. Georgia requires a general-election majority or December runoff; fields are normally two-candidate.

actors.name: Brian Jack (R)
actors.public: First-term incumbent with Trump backing and strong fundraising; won 2024 general easily.
actors.private: Comfortable; focused on House committee work and avoiding a primary challenge.

actors.name: Democratic nominee
actors.public: Little-known challenger; Democrats won around a third of the vote here in 2024.
actors.private: No path to victory; improves margin at best in a Democratic-leaning midterm.

actors.name: Georgia ballot-access regime
actors.public: Steep petition requirements keep minor parties off House ballots.
actors.private: Makes a sub-50 percent winner nearly impossible absent a write-in or independent surge.

events.name: Independent or minor-party candidate on ballot

3592023.background: Louisiana adopted closed party primaries for congressional races starting 2026, with the November election between party nominees plus any independents. LA-05 (northeast Louisiana) is safely Republican; Rep. Julia Letlow is running for US Senate against Bill Cassidy with Trump's endorsement, opening the seat. Louisiana v. Callais may alter district maps.

actors.name: Republican nominee
actors.public: Winner of the GOP closed primary in a district Trump carried by roughly 30 points.
actors.private: Expects easy November win; concern is whether residual rules or map changes produce a multi-candidate November ballot.

actors.name: Louisiana Legislature and Secretary of State
actors.public: Implemented closed primaries (2024 law) and adjusted 2026 election calendar amid Callais litigation.
actors.private: Would redraw maps rapidly to gain seats if the Supreme Court weakens VRA Section 2; may shift dates.

actors.name: US Supreme Court
actors.public: Reheard Louisiana v. Callais on whether race-based districting under VRA Section 2 is constitutional.
actors.private: Ruling could force or permit redistricting that changes candidates and dates in 2026.

events.name: Callais ruling triggers new map or calendar change affecting LA-05
Multiple independents/minor-party candidates crowd November ballot

3592027.background: LA-02 (New Orleans-Baton Rouge) is a safe Democratic, majority-Black seat held by Rep. Troy Carter. Louisiana moved to closed party primaries for Congress in 2026. The Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais case could invalidate race-conscious districts and prompt a mid-cycle redraw targeting Democratic seats.

actors.name: Troy Carter (D)
actors.public: Incumbent since 2021, wins general elections with about 60-70 percent; establishment Democrat.
actors.private: Fears a redraw that merges or dismantles his district or forces a member-versus-member fight with Cleo Fields.

actors.name: Louisiana Republican Legislature / Gov. Jeff Landry
actors.public: Seeks maps favouring Republicans; supported challenge to the second Black-majority district.
actors.private: Would quickly redraw to eliminate a Democratic seat if Callais allows; may alter calendar.

actors.name: US Supreme Court
actors.public: Reheard Callais in October 2025 on VRA Section 2 constitutionality.
actors.private: A broad ruling could reshape Louisiana maps and the 2026 calendar.

events.name: Calendar change postpones or restructures November round

3659919.background: Amapá governor Clécio Luís (Solidariedade), allied with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre and Lula, seeks re-election. Macapá mayor Antônio 'Dr.' Furlan (MDB), re-elected in 2024 with about 85 percent, is the main challenger. Runoff applies if no majority on October 4.

actors.private: Must resign as mayor by April 2026; needs to dominate Macapá and avoid being outspent by state machine.

actors.name: Clécio Luís
actors.public: Incumbent governor backed by Alcolumbre and federal government resources; former Macapá mayor himself.
actors.private: Relies on Alcolumbre's federal leverage and interior towns; aims to force a runoff and consolidate.

actors.name: Davi Alcolumbre
actors.public: Senate President, dominant Amapá power broker.
actors.private: Will deploy federal funds and alliances to stop Furlan, a rival to his hegemony.

Corruption investigation hits a main candidate

3659958.background: Mato Grosso do Sul governor Eduardo Riedel, elected 2022 (PSDB, later moved to PP), seeks re-election in an agribusiness, right-leaning state. actors.name: PL / Bolsonarista base

actors.private: Could field own candidate if deals on Senate slots fail.

3659986.background: Mato Grosso governor Mauro Mendes (União) is term-limited. Senator Wellington Fagundes (PL) seeks the governorship; Vice-Governor Otaviano Pivetta, backed by Mendes, is the main rival. Bolsonarista and agribusiness-dominated state; runoff if no majority.

events.name: Corruption scandal touching the state government
